channel.title: Erv's Notebook
channel.description: Short reflections on Scripture, physics, and the space where they meet.

item.title: Read It in the Order It Happened
item.description: A one-year chronological Bible reading plan: Job inside Genesis, the Psalms inside David's life, the prophets speaking into their own kings and crises. Set your start date and begin.

item.title: God Draws Near. Part 3.
item.description: The finale: God's nearness in the wilderness and the Promised Land, and why the Temple was never the final step — the dwelling place was always headed for human hearts.

item.title: God Draws Near. Part 2.
item.description: The golden calf, and the hardest sentence in Exodus: 'I will not go with you.' Why the accurate word is not that God wanted to destroy His people — but that He must.

item.title: God Draws Near
item.description: The overall message of the Bible in one line: a lovesick Father desperately looking for His children to bring them home. Part 1 — from the Garden to the captivity, with the whole story of God's presence in one table.

item.title: The Journey of the Soul
item.description: The epilogue to The Soul series: an allegory in eight panels, inspired by The Picture of Dorian Gray — but here the portrait is real. A life lived shapes the soul it becomes.

item.title: Late Bloomers
item.description: For my son: Carl Jung on the people the world calls late bloomers — the illusion of falling behind, the work of individuation, and a different kind of intelligence unfolding on a different kind of clock.

item.title: Soul. Spurgeon.
item.description: Closing the Soul series with the Prince of Preachers: Spurgeon's sermon on Mark 8:36 as an interactive podcast, plus seventeen slides running the ultimate audit of the human soul.

item.title: Your Rewards in Heaven. Not Intel.
item.description: Intel's Ranking and Rating rewarded what you did alone — never what you did for the team. I once proposed fixing that with two raises. God, it turns out, already does.

item.title: The Soul: The Series
item.description: The hub for the Soul series — every installment in reading order, the Hebrew and Greek word studies behind it, and the prelude written years before the series had a name.

item.title: Your Soul. The 3 Things.
item.description: In The Soul I argued you only have two decisions in life: where your soul spends eternity, and in what condition. I asked what I might be missing — and there is a third thing: your motives.

item.title: Note to Self
item.description: How a black-and-white engineer learned to embrace paradox — and why my Theory of Everything breakthrough might be that the two theories never needed to be linked at all.

item.title: It's All About Duality
item.description: Nine pairs of opposites I see everywhere — from Relativity vs Quantum Mechanics to Body vs Soul. I asked an AI whether they should be unified or left alone, and the answer was too good to keep to myself.

item.title: 2 Realms. Ask for Yourself.
item.description: God vs Science — the longest-running debate there is. I made an interactive podcast where you can join, ask your questions out loud, and hear the hosts answer in real time.

item.title: The Dust and the Throne
item.description: The written analysis behind the slide study: a title that means both mortal dust (Ezekiel) and enthroned deity (Daniel 7), and the trial where the two collided.

item.title: Son of Man. Son of God.
item.description: Why did Jesus bypass every grand title to call himself the Son of Man? A visual walk from Ezekiel's dust to Daniel's throne — fifteen NotebookLM slides with my notes between them.

item.title: The Soul
item.description: You are an eternal living soul who only ever has to make two real decisions — where it spends eternity, and in what condition. A flowchart, an AI sanity check, and two companion Hebrew/Greek word studies.

item.title: Making Light of Christ
item.description: A quick NotebookLM-generated podcast and slide deck on Making Light of Christ, shared here as a test of how these links look on the blog.

item.title: Becoming a Mormon
item.description: Mormon missionaries have been visiting weekly for five months, and unlike a combative dorm-room debate decades ago, this time felt different — plus the actual checklist of steps required to become a Mormon.

item.title: What Question Is God Asking You Right Now?
item.description: A curated list of the questions God asks in the Old Testament and Jesus asks in the New Testament.

item.title: Hebrew/Greek Interlinear in YouVersion
item.description: A Chrome extension that puts a live Hebrew/Greek interlinear on top of any online study Bible, plus a Koine Greek study update.

item.title: Most Impactful Book of the Bible?
item.description: Wrapping up a year-long study of Revelation, plus building a custom Koine Greek Learning Coach AI Agent.

item.title: God and Breathing
item.description: A 30-second video reframes ruach and pneuma — the Hebrew and Greek words for breath, wind, and spirit.

item.title: Do Not Be Unbelieving, But Believing
item.description: Building a courtroom case for God's existence using actual categories of legal evidence, alongside a chart of the resurrection witnesses' belief journeys.

item.title: What More Proof Do You Need?
item.description: Doubting Thomas needed to touch the nail marks to believe. A meditation on faith, evidence, and 'many infallible proofs' from Acts 1:3.

item.title: Keep the Words of This Prophecy
item.description: A BSF Revelation study question sends Erv into a meditation on the New Jerusalem, judging angels, and a Revelation obedience cheat sheet.

item.title: Holy Week
item.description: A walk through the Holy Week timeline from Palm Sunday to Easter, landing on Spy Wednesday — a meditation on being a forgiven Judas, a Yancey recommendation, and a Spurgeon sermon on the Trinity.

item.title: God is a Hypocrite. Twain
item.description: A Facebook friend posts Mark Twain's famous 'God is a hypocrite' polemic. Rather than debate it in the comments, a full point-by-point response — and why holiness and love, not raw power, are the standard God actually judges Himself by.

item.title: My Inductive Bible Study App
item.description: ChatGPT-5 lands and gets put straight to work building a Bible study web app with Observation, Interpretation, Correlation, and Application boxes, auto-save, and Believer's Bible Commentary built in.

item.title: Heaven. Part 2
item.description: Picking back up open questions from an earlier post on heaven — reigning, judging angels, pilgrimages to the New Jerusalem — plus a Randy Alcorn recommendation and a Mind Map connecting Eden to eternity.

item.title: Creator Cause
item.description: An AI debate on causal versus contingent causes for the universe, a physicist's admission that we don't know why the universe began ordered, and why 'Quantum AI is the creator' collapses under its own logic.

item.title: Which saint are you?
item.description: An AI quiz says Mother Teresa. A reflection on the Apostle's Creed as a litmus test, 40+ years of youth ministry with hurting teenagers, and the very different saint he's become post-tumor.

item.title: Omnipresent. Omniloving
item.description: A short, jokey BSF-day reflection on loving God's attributes, and a wish that science could someday 'prove' Omniloving the way it claims to prove Omnipresence.

item.title: Acts 2
item.description: Studying the Old Testament in Greek to catch New Testament parallels invisible in Hebrew-only comparison, sparked by a Stephen Hackett video on why Pentecost was more explosive than you think.

item.title: Septuagint. LXX
item.description: A 67th-birthday update on the Septuagint-inspiration question, a Stephen Hackett video making the case for adding Correlation to the inductive method, and a step-by-step walkthrough of studying Isaiah 7:14 across Hebrew, Greek, and English.

item.title: Septuagint vs Tanakh
item.description: Wrestling with Joshua's conquest narratives, a virgin-birth translation question in Isaiah 7:14, and a growing doubt about whether the Septuagint carries the same authority as the Hebrew Old Testament.

item.title: Are you Luffing or Bluffing?
item.description: An old essay on what it really means to 'be filled with the Spirit,' borrowed from a sailing metaphor: luffing sails, telltales, and staying oriented to the wind.

item.title: My Decision Matrix App
item.description: Wrestling ChatGPT-assisted Python code through tkinter, Pyinstaller, and PythonAnywhere, with an eye toward eventually turning it into a Bible verse screensaver.

item.title: Bible Clock
item.description: A crowdfunded Bible Clock finally goes into production, and an offer to buy one for anyone in the group who wants it.

item.title: What Displeases God?
item.description: AI wrote an 8-week sermon series and Erv posted it to his Weebly page, one caption-hover image at a time.

item.title: Why the Church?
item.description: An honest look at the 'artificial church' Erv built for himself after brain surgery, why it isn't a real substitute, and an AI-written sermon worth reading anyway.

item.title: Holly's Lecture
item.description: A Sunday check-in on whether a national tragedy might be sparking spiritual revival, and Holly's lecture turned into an AI-narrated slide overview.

item.title: Exile & Return
item.description: The lesson e-book finally lands, and a few things that jumped out ahead of a new BSF year through Ezra, Nehemiah, Daniel, Esther, and the minor prophets.

item.title: BSF Template
item.description: A great first night back with the group, an honest word about the pre-study jitters, and a Google Sheets template for tracking Discussion Question answers all year.

item.title: Chess Master
item.description: BSF starts tomorrow, and a quick walkthrough of NotebookLM's new Video Overview feature using the book of Ezekiel.

item.title: 2 Cor 1:8-9
item.description: On enduring beyond what feels endurable, the heresy hiding inside a popular Christian saying, and stopping the reliance on self to learn reliance on God alone.

item.title: Ecclesiastes. Screensaver
item.description: A Python screensaver for favorite quotes, why Ecclesiastes might be the most intellectually honest book in the Bible, and one week to go before Exile & Return.

item.title: Questioning God
item.description: A month out from Exile & Return, selling the old Jeep, faithfully pre-studying all eight books, and an honest look back at the angry things once said to God — and how Malachi answers them.

item.title: Exile and Return. Podcast
item.description: Deciding to formally join the BSF group this year after a strange confirmation, plus how the AI-narrated podcasts are landing differently than reading the text alone.

item.title: Receive the Word. How?
item.description: A dense reflection on the many ways God communicates beyond the written page, an Abridged/Focused Method framework for hearing His voice, and what it means to sanctify the Lord in your heart.

item.title: Exile and Return. Whetting
item.description: Prepping for BSF's Exile & Return with AI-generated podcasts constrained to Scripture alone, a favorite Logos handbook, and a genuine question about why only Judah returned.

item.title: Free Seminary Classes. DTS
item.description: A quiet summer break from BSF, a great birthday with the grandkids, and a free Dallas Theological Seminary course worth every Christian's time.

item.title: Video Shorts
item.description: Digitizing sixteen years of a Christian library, and nine short reels worth watching.

item.title: Sola Scriptura?
item.description: What Sola Scriptura actually means, the difference between Bible 'resources' and Bible 'books,' and why all truth is God's truth.

item.title: Checkmate
item.description: God as the Master Chess player in the cosmic war with Satan — willing to sacrifice a piece to win the whole game.

item.title: A Model Employee
item.description: What Eliezer, Daniel, and Nehemiah can teach us about being faithful to an earthly authority while staying loyal to God first.

item.title: Miracles
item.description: Does God still do miracles today, and what does it mean to have faith either way? A look at Daniel's furnace and the two camps Christians tend to fall into.

item.title: Nebuchadnezzar vs. Belshazzar
item.description: Two Babylonian kings, two very different responses to God's judgment.

item.title: Fear. Afraid.
item.description: On connection as the underlying theme of the Bible, Ezekiel's terrifying vision, and the paradox of fearing the God who loves you most.

item.title: Ezekiel, the Dung Prophet
item.description: What word clouds reveal about Ezekiel's obsession with idols, the Hebrew word gillulim, and why 'One' might be the single most important word in the Bible.

item.title: A FAT Christian
item.description: On being Faithful, Available, and Teachable — and why God sometimes has to flatten us first.

item.title: Daniel 9
item.description: On memorizing Daniel 9 in college, the ongoing quest to learn Koine Greek, and a Grok prompt for building a real study plan.

item.title: Sovereignty vs. Free Will
item.description: A wide-ranging reflection on suffering, sovereignty, and why Jesus's own suffering matters — with a detour through Daniel's dreams and cosmic warfare.

item.title: Anguish in Prayer
item.description: On bearable pain and unbearable pain, and seven ways prayer works on us even when it doesn't change our circumstances.

item.title: AI, Hebrew, and Greek
item.description: Following up on yesterday's AI Bible study post with a real attempt at using AI for original-language insight on Galatians 5.

item.title: AI Bible Study
item.description: A personal history of Bible-study resources — from Strong's Concordance to Logos to AI — and a simple method for using AI to study a passage.

item.title: Christian USA
item.description: On what church is actually for, Nehemiah's wall-building under opposition, and whether America was ever really a Christian nation.

item.title: Timeline of the OT
item.description: Building a genealogical timeline of Old Testament saints in Google Sheets, one bar chart at a time.

item.title: Thy Will
item.description: On the Holy Spirit as our Comforter, and the sobering biblical pattern of God's judgment being simply to give people exactly what they asked for.

item.title: Hell
item.description: A birthday reflection on John Piper's answers about why we read the Bible, and a small illustration about the real difference between Heaven and Hell.

item.title: The Bible. Connected
item.description: Happy BSF day: an overview of the whole Bible with its story-arc timeline, plus every place in Scripture where Jesus appears or is presented as God.

item.title: Bible Study Resources
item.description: A running list of the books, sites, charts, and timelines I actually trust and keep coming back to for Bible study.

item.title: Christianity makes no sense
item.description: A viral video calling Christians idiots reopened an old wound about being 'the dumb engineer who believes fairy tales' — so I sat down and answered all 17 of its accusations.

item.title: Christianity vs. other religions
item.description: AI dodged the ten worldview questions everyone eventually has to answer — until I pushed back with what my Worldviews class had already taught me.

item.title: What is a Scribe?
item.description: An extemporaneous voice conversation with AI about Ezra's 900-mile journey turned into a real study of what it meant to be both a scribe and a priest.

item.title: The joy of our Master
item.description: What does 'enter into the joy of your master' in Matthew 25 actually mean — a small phrase that turns out to carry an entire theology of heaven.

item.title: God and Science
item.description: A pet peeve about 'God and Science are incompatible' turns into a two-picture argument for why the universe's elements and their rules need an explanation science alone can't give.

item.title: Believe vs. Belief
item.description: A 4am question about how much you have to believe in Christ to be saved leads into the Greek word for belief, and a betting analogy that finally made it click.

item.title: Myths and Fairy Tales
item.description: A missed word in Mark 4, and the story of how Tolkien convinced C.S. Lewis that Christianity is the one true myth.

item.title: David's throne
item.description: BSF asks whether Ezekiel's prophecy of David's throne points to Christ or to David himself — Scripture's own pattern of type and fulfillment settles it for me.

item.title: Prayer Bear
item.description: A 4am prayer, a Care Bear quoting Galatians, and a Greek word study on what it really means to bear one another's burdens.

item.title: His yoke is easy?
item.description: Salvation is all Him. But almost everything else God does with us runs on partnership — a small table tracing what He asks of us against what He does Himself, from Adam to David.

item.title: The Bible. Timeline.
item.description: Every person, place, and event in the Bible, linked to time — the data is finished, the chart just needs to become readable.

item.title: The Bible. Charts. Maps. Timelines.
item.description: Feeding my whole Bible timeline database to AI with zero instructions produced a surprisingly good survey of the Old Testament — proof there's more to this project than I expected.

item.title: The Law(s). For a NT Christian.
item.description: A 4am question about whether Christians should keep the Old Testament Law splits into three very different answers depending on which law you mean.

item.title: MY OT Explorer App
item.description: A running list of every Bible resource I trust, now built into the footer of my OT Explorer app — Wiersbe, Spurgeon, and a dozen others.

item.title: Satan. Smarter than a Third Grader?
item.description: If crucifying Christ was Satan's plan, it might be the single dumbest move in the history of his war against God.

item.title: Jewish genocide
item.description: Three thousand years of attempts to destroy Israel, and Israel is still here. To me, that's not just history — it's evidence.

item.title: Children in sex slavery
item.description: A hard BSF discussion question about taking a stand like Esther led me back into research on child trafficking I hadn't looked at in years.

item.title: deGrasse. The universe thinks you are nothing.
item.description: Neil deGrasse Tyson set out to prove humanity is cosmically insignificant. He's right about the numbers, and exactly backwards about what they mean.

item.title: Plato. Theory of Forms. Allegory of the Cave.
item.description: Wondering how the spiritual realm and the physical world relate to each other led me straight into Plato's cave — and out again, with a Christian correction.

item.title: My ISI website
item.description: I never paid attention to the traffic on my ISI site until now — 1,500+ unique visitors in 90 days made me wonder if there's a ministry left in me after all.

item.title: God. Angels. Man.
item.description: A 3am chart comparing what God, angels, and humans before and after the Fall can and can't do — and a reminder that Satan's real opposite isn't God.

item.title: Leanness in your soul
item.description: Israel got exactly what they demanded in the wilderness — and Psalm 106 says that was the problem.

item.title: Bible App. VOD.
item.description: After fifteen years of collecting Bible resources, a simple Verse of the Day app has become the one I keep coming back to.

item.title: Encouragement
item.description: A note on Barnabas — the 'Son of Encouragement' — ahead of tonight's Q10 discussion.

item.title: Haggai
item.description: A quick link to help see the big picture of Haggai before our next Discussion.

item.title: God’s negative attributes
item.description: Severity, wrath, jealousy, anger — attributes that sound alarming in a person read very differently once you see what they actually mean in God.

item.title: Politics
item.description: A conversation with my daughter about why politics drives me crazy, and a Far Side cartoon that says more about infinity than most Cosmology textbooks.

item.title: Consciousness
item.description: Roger Penrose's technical case for what consciousness actually is landed somewhere I've been circling for years — and it keeps God, not chance, at the center.

item.title: Fruit
item.description: Fruit is the first thing God ever says to us in the Bible, and He never lets up on the theme — Hosea finally showed me why.

item.title: Dance with the Spirit.
item.description: A conversation with my pastor about revival got me wondering whether 'walk by the Spirit' might carry more rhythm than we usually give it credit for.

item.title: The Bible. Overview.
item.description: Two pet projects finished: a book-by-book overview of the whole Bible with a timeline, and a running list of every place Jesus appears or is presented as God.

item.title: The Bible interprets itself. Correlation.
item.description: One image says it better than I could — every cross-reference in Scripture, arced from Genesis to Revelation.

item.title: Creation. Day 4
item.description: Two videos on the Hebrew of Genesis's fourth day of creation left me saying 'wow' out loud, more than once.

item.title: The Baditudes
item.description: The Beatitudes are easier to feel the weight of once you set them against their mirror image — Jesus's own list of woes to the Pharisees.

item.title: Heaven
item.description: Turning 68, and having survived a life-threatening brain tumor, prompts an honest first pass at hard questions about what heaven actually is.

item.title: The Third Commandment
item.description: What "you shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain" actually means in Hebrew — and why it's about far more than profanity.

item.title: Quantum Mechanics Meets God
item.description: Could the strangest ideas in quantum mechanics — the observer effect, entanglement, non-locality — echo something ancient theology has claimed about God all along?

item.title: Bang!
item.description: Having some fun with AI comparing Genesis 1 to the Big Bang — plus a serious 33-minute watch on Einstein, God, and science.

item.title: Psalm 91
item.description: Turning Psalm 91's promises of God's protection into a single image, to absorb more of what the words were describing.

item.title: 50 Questions
item.description: A cheap Logos sale find with 50 questions worth wrestling with — plus a bonus deep-dive into the Hebrew word Shalom.

item.title: The Trinity. Roles & Responsibilities.
item.description: One God, three persons, one will — sketching who does what in creation and salvation, and why calling the Spirit 'more sensitive' undersells all three.

item.title: Other Religions
item.description: Months of weekly conversations with Mormon missionaries, and a comparison chart built to sort out where the real differences actually lie.

item.title: Prepared. But for What?
item.description: Why doesn't God take us to heaven the instant we choose Him? A working theology of earth as preparation, built while writing a children's book.

item.title: The 10 Commandments. Outdated?
item.description: Which of the Ten Commandments does modern culture still treat as clearly wrong to break — and which ones have quietly become optional?

item.title: Zech 11:4-17. ICB.
item.description: Reading Zechariah's parable of the foolish shepherd in the International Children's Bible, and why it hit the same nerve as Ezekiel 34 and Nehemiah's tears.

item.title: Fasting
item.description: Years of fasting for the right reasons, and a video that still found room to convict me — plus Isaiah 58's warning about fasting that never leaves the room.

item.title: Leanness
item.description: A pattern in Scripture where the worst judgment isn't withholding what we want, but granting it.

item.title: Zech 5:3
item.description: A Hebrew word study on naqah — the 'clean' or 'innocent' declared guiltless — traced across Exodus, Numbers, Nahum, and Zechariah.

item.title: Pray for Cori. AI.
item.description: A prayer of healing shaped by Scripture's promises, offered for a friend's daughter.

item.title: Confessing Sin. Of Others.
item.description: Learning to mourn the sins of my people the way Daniel, Nehemiah, and Ezra did — without pretending guilt that isn't mine.

item.title: Is There a God? Why Read the Bible?
item.description: Two shorter, shareable summaries: spotting the logical gaps in a popular argument against God, and why Scripture needs to be constantly in us.
